indicators.section: Red Flags: Indicia of Sham Transactions
indicators.flag: Commercially unreasonable transactions.  Transfers of property in which a blocked person once held an interest on terms that are not commercially reasonable, lacking adequate consideration, or otherwise not suggestive of an arm’s length transaction may indicate that the blocked person still retains an interest in the property.
indicators.red_flag: Below-market / non-arm's-length asset transfer (sham-divestment of blocked interest)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D18 (Real-estate / property & valuation data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Red Flags: Indicia of Sham Transactions
indicators.flag: Transfer  to  family  members  or  close  associates.    Transfers  by  a  blocked  person  to  a  family member or close associate can be evidence of a sham transaction.  Such family members or close associates may be acting as a proxy, facilitator, money manager, or agent for the blocked person.
indicators.red_flag: Asset transfer to family / close-associate nominee acting as sanctioned-party proxy
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C17 (PEP & sanctioned-elite proxy screening).

indicators.section: Red Flags: Indicia of Sham Transactions
indicators.flag: Unclear purpose of transfer.  Transfers lacking apparent business purpose may indicate an attempt to obfuscate a blocked person’s continued interest in property.  Likewise, transfers to an individual with little or no relevant experience or expertise with respect to the transferred property may be evidence of a sham transaction.
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Red Flags: Indicia of Sham Transactions
indicators.flag: Unduly  complex  corporate  structures  involving  higher-risk  jurisdictions.    The  presence  of unnecessarily  complex  legal  structures  without  a  discernible  legitimate  purpose—such  as  certain multi-layered limited liability companies, partnerships, or trusts—may indicate an effort to conceal an ownership interest.
indicators.red_flag: Multi-layered shell / trust structure in secrecy jurisdiction (UBO concealment)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Red Flags: Indicia of Sham Transactions
indicators.flag: Continued involvement of a blocked person.  Facts or circumstances suggesting a blocked person remains involved in the use, management, or disposition of property—including through proxies or intermediaries—may indicate that the blocked person continues to retain an interest in property.
indicators.red_flag: Sanctioned party retains control via proxy after nominal divestment
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C17 (PEP & sanctioned-elite proxy screening).

indicators.section: Red Flags: Indicia of Sham Transactions
indicators.flag: Transfer near the time of designation. Transfers completed close in time to a person’s designation may trigger suspicion warranting further analysis, such as when a purported transfer occurs
indicators.red_flag: Asset transfer in close temporal proximity to OFAC designation event
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C18 (Sanctions / watchlist screening).

indicators.section: Red Flags: Indicia of Sham Transactions
indicators.flag: Evasive  responses  regarding  a  blocked  person’s  involvement.    Evasive  or  vague  responses,  or failures to respond to questions from counterparties, key intermediaries, or gatekeepers regarding a blocked person’s involvement in property may be evidence of intent to conceal a continuing interest.
indicators.red_flag: Evasive / non-responsive answers on blocked-person involvement (KYC non-cooperation)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.
